A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlashCache research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support comparison. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, compression and latency measurements, cutoff and budget-allocation ablations, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds MathVista evaluation, further ablations, outlier-removal experiments and long-sequence overhead measurements.

M1.justification: The substantive procedure remains DCT-based filtering, IDCT reconstruction, MSE-based outlier selection and frequency-energy-based budget allocation. Appendix B explicitly clarifies retention of decoding KVs, consistent with v1's single post-prefill compression operation. No new component or changed inference schedule is established.

E1.justification: Appendix B and Table 9 add MathVista with chain-of-thought reasoning, extending evaluation to a reasoning-heavy, long-generation scenario. The existing multi-image, high-resolution and video benchmarks remain covered.

E2.justification: The new MathVista comparison includes VLCache, Quest and PyramidKV, which were not evaluated as comparators in v1. They supplement the retained StreamingLLM, H2O, SnapKV, LOOK-M and MEDA methods. Comparator membership in the existing experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: New settings include MathVista(CoT) with Qwen2.5-VL-7B at retention ratio 0.1, LLaVA cutoff testing, and per-layer method-overhead comparisons at 32K/64K with a prefilling-time reference. The earlier method-overhead comparison covered 2K-8K. Existing experiment settings are retained; the narrower recommended cutoff range does not establish a change to their actual settings.

E4.justification: Table 10 extends cutoff sensitivity analysis from Qwen to LLaVA-OneVision-8B. New Figure 11 extends the targeted-removal analysis across model architectures, parameter scales and datasets, testing whether removing high-deviation KVs remains especially damaging. These supplement the retained ablations and frequency-distribution analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for these experiments. The additional results retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing numerical tables are retained. New results include MathVista scores of 52.6 for FlashCache, 51.6 for MEDA and 68.2 for Full Cache; additional cutoff and removal curves; and FlashCache overheads of 12.45/28.12 ms at 32K/64K, with all four tested latency baselines reporting OOM at 64K. These are supplementary results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Equation 8 changes the zeroed-frequency branch from omega <= m to omega < m, removing its overlap with the retained branch at the cutoff. The remaining mathematical development is unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same frequency-domain novelty, attention-score-free and training-free compression claims, including up to 1.69x decoding speedup with 80% lower KV memory. Additional experiments support existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 4.6 narrows the preferred cutoff range from 0.1-0.3 to 0.1-0.2. Appendix C adds an explanation involving Base KV overfitting at large cutoffs; Appendices D.3 and E interpret new evidence as supporting broader outlier generality and long-context memory stability. The limitations paragraph is unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B makes full retention of decoding KVs explicit, clarifying the previously described compression schedule. The new acknowledgments identify Fudan's CFFF computing platform. The H200 GPU, FlashAttention and CuPy implementation disclosures remain unchanged, with no new code or data access instructions.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to EMR-Merging, Think Twice, Act Once, beta-DARTS++, and Dynamic Model Merging with Mixture of Weights. The research positioning remains substantially unchanged. Consolidating the two ZipVL entries retains that work rather than removing it.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose is retained. Author affiliations and contribution notes are updated, acknowledgments are added, and the appendix outline gains sections and short explanatory passages. This is a localized expansion rather than extensive rewriting or narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 9-11 and the four-panel Figure 11. Earlier Tables 9 and 8 become Tables 8 and 12, respectively, and the case-study Figure 11 becomes Figure 12. Existing displays are retained with resizing, spacing and placement adjustments.

improvement.justification: The cross-model cutoff/removal checks and 32K/64K overhead comparisons address limited gaps in v1's evidence for generality and scalability. MathVista adds useful evidence of both a relative advantage over tested compression methods and a remaining full-cache accuracy gap. Together with the Equation 8 correction, these modestly improve the paper, although sparse new-protocol details and unchanged uncertainty reporting limit the gain.
